Nordea's late-quarter MtM hit and tighter CET1 headroom for a full 1.0% buyback lean slightly negative against a conservative impairment bar and a likely restructuring-saving quantification; a 17-analyst bank with the one-offs pre-released, so near zero.

Arctic 5% above consensus, a rental-income bar set below Q2's 902m, Atrium Ljungberg's unchanged yields and a held Riksbank rate all argue the Q3 numbers cannot show the rate damage a 17% drawdown to a 52-week low is braced for; shorts covering.

The company's own KPI workbook shows a cash-product mix shift that puts commission per trade under what the 15-Oct consensus implies, and consensus FY NI sits in the upper part of a guide the company will have to place at Q3; offset by EUR 1.5m of insider buying and a pending EUR 100m buyback on a stock already -34% in 60 days.

Draeger's ad-hoc Q3 pre-release (medical sales -1.4%, orders -3.0%) is a negative read-through to Acute Care against a +9.5% ventilator comp, on a stock sitting at the mean target after +36% from the insider buys; partly offset by the ex-refund margin trend and USD/SEK.

Wallenstam's unchanged residential yields and +578m derivative gain point to a value line better than the -20.8m that cost 2.6% last year, and the buyback program is four sessions from its cap with mandate room to 10%; unsourced bar, thin name.

A 9M guidance nudge above '>8%' is plausible on the company's own 'comfortably' language and the 9M25 precedent, but the last two upgrades were sold and spot sits above the average target; no register, so the lean is the run-up.

SB1 models 334m adj. EBITA, 6% over a consensus that undershot Q2 by 14%, Stena bought SEK 430m mid-quarter with board access, and the +16% backlog supports volumes; this name moves double digits on margin either way, so input-cost pressure keeps p_up modest.

JM's own Q3/Q2 revenue ratios (0.70-0.84x) put Q3 revenue at 1,970-2,365 against a 2,544 consensus that implies 0.90x, no investor-project sale was filed this quarter against a 205-unit sale in the comp, and consensus margin assumes no seasonal dip after two prints that missed EBIT by 55% and 39% and fell 12%; the 11.7% short and the +8% five-day run-up keep it from being larger.

A company that pre-released its Q1 and H1 misses within days of quarter-end issued no Q3 update 20 days after it, while the stock fell 23% on no news; SatCom order silence and a report-day history of -8/-13/-4.75% keep the lean small on a $0.1m microcap.

The 216m sales bar implies organic growth halving from Q2's +42% while the company's own two-year stack plus USD/SEK and Koroyd gives ~225-230m, the 9.48% short is building into the print (Marshall Wace doubled since September) and the last three sales beats were bought +28%, +9% and +11%; the strongest case on the day.

The stock rose 12.8% into the print to meet Handelsbanken's +11% organic order forecast while Nederman's own seasonality points to about +4%, on a name that sold four of its last five reports; backlog conversion supports sales but sales is not the line it trades on.

ABG's lukewarm preview is already in a stock down 13% in 20 days and the backlog note gives slight H2 upside, but the order book prints ~550 vs 668, the headline that sank two of the last four reports; the findings offset to zero.

H1 adjusted EBITA grew 46% with Laydex and Arvid Nilsson now consolidating, while the only public estimate implies H2 at just +16%, and Byggmax (+5.1% LFL) and Clas Ohlson (+12% organic) printed the day before on a $150k name with one broker; leverage and lagged FX are the small drags.

H1 cloud revenue at +26% cc leaves H2 needing only 19.6-23.3% for the FY range and the CCB bar (24.7%) sits below the 25-26% run-rate Reltio still feeds, but the stock is +58% off the July low at the consensus target, so the ADR-implied ~6.5% move is nearly symmetric.

Management's pre-close guided Q3 NII headwinds 'similar to Q2', when NII was flat, yet the 19-Oct consensus still models +1.7% q/q; the Q2 NII miss cost 3.5%, and Nordea's fair-value hit puts the 516m NFT line at risk, partly offset by the recurring cost and credit-loss beats.

A third weak operating cash flow from separation working capital has no consensus line and sank the last two prints, stranded costs sit in the first continuing-ops margin, and the name has fallen on four straight reports; PMI and Fastenal support the 3.6% organic bar but are partly in it.

Q3 and the guide cut were pre-released the day before and the stock fell 12% for an ~11% EBIT-midpoint cut, more than July's 8.4% for a 13% cut, where the next session bounced +4.1%; a one-analog overshoot against a leverage line near 3x and a selling 15% holder.
